text:
Cheap fuel, costly surrender

Trump’s fuel deal with Putin is a disgraceful retreat dressed up as economic leadership. It offers Moscow the prospect of renewed revenue while asking everyone else to believe that cheaper diesel justifies weakening pressure on a government still waging war against Ukraine.

The European Union’s foreign-policy chief, Kaja Kallas, put the objection plainly: suspending sanctions on Russian diesel gives Moscow more money to wage war. “This is not the time to ease pressure on Russia,” she said, “and Europe won’t.” That is the central issue - not the sales pitch about lower prices, but who gets paid and what that money enables.

Germany has reaffirmed its sanctions policy. Britain says it will maintain pressure on Russia. Australia has rejected Russian fuel, with Energy Minister Chris Bowen declaring: “We don’t need or want Russian fuel in Australia.” These governments are refusing to treat Putin’s export earnings as an acceptable solution to Washington’s fuel problem.

That makes Trump’s decision look less like a diplomatic breakthrough than a spectacular failure of **judgment**. Sanctions are supposed to impose a cost on aggression. Relaxing them for a fuel deal risks turning that principle upside down: Russia gains a commercial opening while the countries supporting Ukraine are left defending the pressure Washington is helping to undermine.

And you would think you’d have your shit together on energy security after all the chest-thumping about controlling Venezuela and its oil. If that is the boast, why is the answer now a deal with Putin? What happened to the supposedly masterful strategy?

The promised economic payoff is not even assured. Analysts quoted in the reporting question Russia’s ability to deliver the advertised supplies and whether the agreement will meaningfully reduce fuel prices. Moscow could gain a concession while consumers are left waiting for the benefit Trump has advertised.

None of this requires pretending every allied leader has publicly condemned Trump. They have not. Australia’s response, for example, deliberately stopped short of condemning the United States. But diplomatic restraint does not make the underlying disagreement disappear: rewarding Russian energy exports while trying to restrain Russia’s war is a contradiction, not a strategy.

Lower fuel prices are a legitimate public goal. They are not a moral blank cheque. A president who sells sanctions relief as strength should explain why Putin gets an economic opening while everyone else gets another promise.

text:
My neighbor offered me $500 a month to stop parking in front of my own house.

I thought he was joking until he handed me an envelope with the first payment.

I live in a quiet neighborhood outside Columbus, Ohio. Most houses have driveways, but the street parking gets tight whenever somebody has visitors.

My neighbor, Dennis, moved in about eight months ago.

He’s in his late 50s, keeps his lawn ridiculously neat, and has a habit of blowing leaves off the sidewalk before they even finish falling.

We’d never had a problem.

Then one Saturday, he knocked on my door.

He asked whether I’d consider parking farther down the street.

I told him I usually parked directly in front of my house because it was convenient.

He said his wife had trouble getting out of their driveway when cars were parked opposite it.

text:
Why your retarded:

1. NEAR’s computational capabilities (not throughput/TPS)
NEAR does not offer general-purpose server-style compute. Smart contracts are compiled to WebAssembly and executed inside a sandboxed Wasmtime virtual machine. Every instruction is metered with gas, so computation is deliberately limited and deterministic. Parallelism comes from sharding (different shards execute independently). This works well for financial logic, state changes, and coordinating agents, but heavy workloads (AI training, large simulations, complex analytics) are expected to stay off-chain or in TEEs.

2. How much of NEAR relies on existing Web2/server tech
There is no official percentage published. In practice:

The core protocol and client (nearcore) are custom.
The contract runtime now uses the standard industry Wasmtime engine.
The large majority of real-world usage (running nodes, RPCs, indexers, explorers, front-ends, and almost all application logic beyond the critical on-chain state) depends on traditional cloud servers and Web2 infrastructure.
Most production Web3 systems, including NEAR, are hybrid: the blockchain handles the shared, trust-minimized state, while everything else leans on existing server and Web2 technology.

What's your defense: is it someday they plan to be entirely onchain? 

I genuinely want to hear your retarded ass rebuttal.....

text:
DRAFT - 3 minute read - A tale of the wizard and the wayward waif.

To live effectively is to live with adequate information. Thus, communication and control belong to the essence of man’s inner life, even as they belong to his life in society.
— Norbert Wiener

And the 21st century might create a massive new class of useless people—people who don’t just have no jobs, but who are unemployable. The same processes that might upgrade humans into gods will also make the rest of people irrelevant.
—Yuval Harari

Norbert Wiener penned a classic on the connection between cybernetics, systems thinking and morality in The Human Use of Human Beings: Cybernetics and Society (1950). As one reviewer put it, “only a few books stand as landmarks in social and scientific upheaval. Norbert Wiener’s classic is one in that small company … Founder of the science of cybernetics, Wiener hoped that machines would release people from relentless and repetitive drudgery in order to achieve more creative pursuits”.

Inventor and futurist Buckminster Fuller echoed this outlook and advocated using advanced technology to free humanity from soul damaging, monotonous work, allowing people to pursue self-directed creative endeavors. For the automation age, he advised “[t]he true business of people should be to go back to school and think about whatever it was they were thinking about before somebody came along and told them they had to earn a living.” 

Futurist Robert Anton Wilson summed up the situation with: “unemployment has no cure because it is not a disease… The requirement for less coerced human work is the natural, healthy functioning of an advanced technological society”. C. H. Douglas, founder of social credit monetary reform, agreed: "The tendency and the proper aim of the economic system is not to create full employment... but to create disemployment; that is to say, to liberate human beings from routine labor." Douglas went on to echo Wiener with: “Systems were made for men, and not men for systems, and the interest of man which is self-development, is above all systems, whether theological, political or economic.” Overall, our technology allows the pursuit of happiness through increased freedom; the lilies of the field come into bloom as it were.

Wiener saw the fork in the road for an automated society long ago when he wrote: “[w]e have contributed to the initiation of a new science which... embraces technical developments with great possibilities for good and for evil…The best we can do is to see that a large public understands the trend and the bearing of the present work.” He held little regard for the capabilities of the obsolete institutions and an over-reliance on automation itself warning: “whether we entrust our decisions to machines of metal, or to those machines of flesh and blood which are bureaus and vast laboratories and armies and corporations, we shall never receive the right answer to our questions.

Wiener also remarked on the capability for human uniqueness, and hence requisite variety. He wrote: "I wish to show that the human individual, capable of vast learning and study, which may occupy almost half of his life, is physically equipped, as the ant is not, for this capacity. Variety and possibility are inherent in the human sensorium—and are indeed the key to man's most noble flights—because variety and possibility belong to the very structure of the human organism." Free will, with free cooperative action, through free speech, breeds requisite variety, the creative spark a key component.

Machines of Metal and Monkey Minds

Wiener, Fuller, Wilson, among others, and many spiritual traditions, see each individual as having the spark of the divine within, something to be nurtured and grown, to bring each and everyone’s bit of creative genius to the celebration of life. That is Wiener’s “great possibilities for good”.On the other hand, Yuval Noah Harari, a prominent voice at the World Economic Forum (WEF), looks at the “evil” side of that equation. He wrote: “we might nevertheless witness the rise of a new useless class … The most important question in twenty-first-century economics may well be what to do with all the superfluous people. What will conscious humans do once we have highly intelligent non-conscious algorithms that can do almost everything better?…One answer might be drugs and computer games ... Unnecessary people might spend increasing amounts of time within 3D virtual-reality worlds that would provide them with far more excitement and emotional engagement than the drab reality outside.” 

Freed from the chains of a monotonous job on an assembly line in a truly drab warehouse or shuffling mainly meaningless paper in a cubicle farm, to go hiking, painting, creating, building, socializing and more is not what springs to mind for the higher ups. The sedation of being hooked up to a fake, shallow, sterile digital world is the solution in Harari’s view.  The great bulk of individuals safely placed where they can be lorded over.

Curtis Yarvin's concepts echo Harari’s. He moves through a small, well-documented network of wealthy backers. Palantir CEO Peter Thiel has called Yarvin one of his most important influences. Palantir builds data-analysis software used by governments and police forces to track people, and it has landed large contracts with the Pentagon, ICE, and other agencies for such surveillance work. That scale of reach has made Palantir a lightning rod for civil rights advocates, who argue the company gives the state tools to watch its own citizens far beyond what oversight can keep up with. Peter Thiel's venture firm, was a lead investor in Flock's $275 million funding round. Flock's network of over 80,000 license-plate cameras across the country has already turned up in cases where federal agencies — including CBP — accessed local Flock data without local officials' knowledge.

Thiel protege and Vice President of the U.S., J. D. Vance has praised Yarvin by name since taking office. Yarvin advocates a country run like a business, owned by shareholders and managed by a single CEO instead of voted on by citizens. He pictures the long-term future as a world broken into thousands of small city-states, each owned outright by its own corporation. Residents get no vote; their only power is to leave for a different city-state if they don't like how they're treated, the same way a customer switches brands. 

Curtis Yarvin offered what he framed as the real, humane solution: seal each person alone in a sealed cell wired to a virtual-reality system, so they'd believe they were living a rich, full life while actually locked away and erased from the world outside — cheaper than prison, he argued, and kinder than killing people outright. 

Today, this vision of 3D virtual-reality worlds is actively taking shape as the “metaverse.” While these corporations pitch the metaverse as the exciting next generation of the internet, Harari’s dark outlook suggests these virtual worlds could simply become a high-tech distraction designed to pacify a population that the elites no longer need. A waste disposal problem as it were. 

The technocratic vision Harari and Yarwin outline aligns closely with the institutional framing of the World Economic Forum. Both promote a narrative where centralized data management, artificial intelligence, and algorithmic governance replace messy, decentralized human self-determination. The WEF champions frameworks like the Fourth Industrial Revolution, which treats society as an optimization problem waiting to be solved through biometric tracking, digital identity, and predictive analytics.

Power Corrupts Reason

When a global elite views humanity through a purely materialist and data-driven lens, top-down management becomes the default preference. The individual is reduced to a node in a networked economy, monitored and directed by administrative systems that claim to know what is best because they process more variables. It is the institutional translation of Harari's thesis. 

Futurist Alvin Toffler foresaw the current elite direction his 1970s Future Shock work where he wrote: "[i]nstead of being stimulated by the challenge, the elites are paralyzed. They retreat into sterile dogmatism. They become unimaginative and frightened. Instead of inventing new social forms, they desperately try to prop up the old ones, applying yesterday's solutions to tomorrow's crises." In this case, hi-tech feudalism and colorful dungeons are part of the past sought.

Disempowerment of the individual is not an unusual stance for those in high positions. Nor is the idea that a person is unnecessary, useless even, once they can no longer serve an elite, as though that were the highest purpose in life. And it is up to these same elites to decide your and my future in life, once we are out from under the thumb of the 9 to 5 grind. At root, this is the mindset that a master would have for a slave. 

There could not be a starker contrast between the current outlook of Harari and cybernetics founder Norbert Wiener, who saw the emerging automation as the key to creating the conditions for freedom and the self-development of each and every individual to their highest potential. It shows how far society has fallen that elites like Harari are presented as the informed seers for the future, and people such as Norbert Wiener are all but unknown; for now. 

The world is waking up to the choice Wiener identified — between technology as liberation and technology as control. History suggests that those who bet against human dignity and creativity ultimately lose, although in previous age transitions, as futurist Alvin Toffler pointed out, great suffering occurred. Toffler’s central mission was ensuring this transition would be different — that for the first time, humanity would navigate an age change with enough foresight and design to spare much of the suffering. That is precisely what just and scientifically informed economics in the way of binary economics, cybernetic feedback helices, and a genuinely informed citizenry make possible. Norbert Wiener was perhaps a bit premature with his warning, when he had written: “The hour is very late, and the choice of good and evil knocks at our door.”

மேடையில் நடந்த அந்த மாஸ் சம்பவம் என்ன? 🤔🎤
செய்தியாளர்கள் அவரிடம், "அமெரிக்காவிடமிருந்து F-35 ஐந்தாம் தலைமுறை ஸ்டெல்த் விமானங்களை இந்தியா வாங்குவது குறித்துப் பேச்சுவார்த்தை நடக்கிறதா?" என்று கேள்வி எழுப்பினர். அதற்கு அவர் கொடுத்த பதில் சும்மா அக்மார்க் நெத்தியடி:

"F-35 விமானத்தை எங்களுக்கு விற்பதற்கு அமெரிக்காவிடமிருந்து இதுவரை எந்த ஒரு அதிகாரப்பூர்வ சலுகையும் (Official Offer) வரவில்லை! பக்கத்தில் உட்கார்ந்திருக்கும் இந்த அமெரிக்க தளபதியிடம் கூட இப்பதான் நான் சொன்னேன்... 'அட போங்கப்பா, உங்க ஆளுங்க எங்களை அந்த விமானத்தின் பக்கத்துல கூட போக விட மாட்டேங்குறாங்க, இதுல அதை எங்களுக்கு விக்கப் போறோம்னு மட்டும் பேச்சு வேற!' அதனால் அப்படி எந்த அதிகாரப்பூர்வ ஆஃபரும் எங்க கைக்கு வரல!"

என்று அமெரிக்காவின் முகமூடியை சிரித்துக்கொண்டே கிழித்துத் தொங்கவிட்டுவிட்டார்!

ரஷ்யாவின் Su-57 ஆஃபர் நிலவரம் என்ன? 🇷🇺🛩️

அமெரிக்காவின் வெற்று உருட்டுகளை உடைத்த அதே வேளையில், ரஷ்யாவின் ஐந்தாம் தலைமுறை ஸ்டெல்த் போர் விமானமான Su-57 குறித்து மிக முக்கியமான ஒரு எதார்த்தத்தைப் பகிர்ந்துகொண்டார்:

📩 ரஷ்யா முன்வைத்த ஆஃபர்: ரஷ்யா தங்களது அதிநவீன Su-57 போர் விமானங்களை இந்தியாவுக்கு வழங்க முன்வந்துள்ள தகவலை ஏர் சீஃப் மார்ஷல் உறுதிப்படுத்தினார்.

⚖️ மதிப்பீட்டு நிலை (Evaluation Pending): ஆனால், அந்த விமானத்தை இந்திய விமானப்படை மதிப்பீடு (Evaluate) செய்ய வேண்டுமா வேண்டாமா என்பதை இந்திய அரசு இன்னும் இறுதி செய்யவில்லை.

🎯 செயல்பாட்டுத் தேவைகள்: அரசாங்கம் அதற்குப் பச்சைக்கொடி காட்டிய பிறகு, ரஷ்யாவின் Su-57 நமது இந்திய வான்படையின் களத் தேவைகளுக்கு (Operational requirements) எந்த அளவிற்குப் பொருந்துகிறது என்பதை நேரில் ஆய்வு செய்து முடிவு எடுப்போம் என்றும், தற்போது அதன் விவரங்கள் பொதுவெளியில் (Open source) உள்ள அளவிற்கே எங்களுக்குத் தெரியும் என்றும் எதார்த்தமாகப் போட்டு உடைத்தார்.

டிஃபென்ஸ் மற்றும் புவிசார் அரசியல் பார்வை -  இதன் முக்கியத்துவம் என்ன?

ஒரு சர்வதேச மற்றும் ராணுவப் பார்வையாளராக இதை நாம் எப்படிப் பார்க்க வேண்டும் என்றால்:

அமெரிக்காவின் 'கட்டுப்பாட்டு' அரசியல் (Strategic Leash):
அமெரிக்காவின் F-35 என்பது வெறும் போர் விமானம் அல்ல; அது வாஷிங்டனின் ரிமோட் கண்ட்ரோல்!

அந்த விமானத்தை வாங்கினாலும் அதன் சாப்ட்வேர் சோர்ஸ் கோடை (Source code) அவர்கள் தர மாட்டார்கள்.

விமானத்தின் மெயின்டனன்ஸுக்குக் கூட அமெரிக்க இன்ஜினியர்களையே நம்பியிருக்க வேண்டும்.

இந்திய அதிகாரிகளைப் பக்கத்திலேயே நெருங்க விடாமல் பூட்டி வைக்கும் ஒரு நாட்டிடம், பில்லியன் கணக்கான டாலர்களைக் கொட்டி ஒரு ஆயுதத்தை வாங்கி நமது கழுத்தை நாமே அவர்களின் கயிற்றில் கொடுக்க இந்தியா ஒருபோதும் தயாராக இல்லை என்பதைத்தான் தளபதியின் வார்த்தைகள் உணர்த்துகின்றன!

ரஷ்யாவின் திறந்த கதவுகள் vs இந்தியாவின் நிதானம்:

மறுபக்கம், ரஷ்யா தனது Su-57 விமானத்தை இந்தியாவுடன் இணைந்து தயாரிக்கவும், தொழில்நுட்பத்தைப் பகிரவும் (Tech transfer) தயாராக இருக்கிறது. இருப்பினும், ஏற்கனவே உக்ரைன் போர்க்களத்தில் Su-57 செயல்பட்ட விதம், அதன் இன்ஜின் தரம் மற்றும் ரேடார் மறைவுத் திறன் (Stealth capabilities) ஆகியவை இந்தியாவின் எதிர்காலத் தேவைகளுக்கு 100% பொருந்துமா என்பதை இந்தியா மிகக் கவனமாக எடைபோட்டு வருகிறது.

நமது இலக்கு உள்நாட்டு AMCA! 🇮🇳🚀:

வெளிநாடுகளிடம் கையேந்துவதை விட, இந்தியா தனது சொந்த ஐந்தாம் தலைமுறை ஸ்டெல்த் போர் விமானமான AMCA (Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft) திட்டத்தை மிகத் தீவிரமாக முன்னெடுத்து வருகிறது. இடையில் இடைக்காலத் தேவைக்காக மட்டுமே இந்த வெளிநாட்டு வாய்ப்புகள் பரிசீலிக்கப்படுகின்றனவே தவிர, யாருடைய காலனித்துவ நிபந்தனைகளுக்கும் இந்தியா பணியாது என்பது தெளிவாகிவிட்டது!

முடிவு: சமரசமற்ற சுயமரியாதை!

அமெரிக்கா எத்தனை ஆயிரம் தடவை F-35 பற்றிப் பிம்பத்தைக் கட்டமைத்தாலும், "தொட்டுப் பார்க்கக் கூட விடாத பொருளை வாங்க நாங்கள் ஒன்றும் ஏமாளிகள் அல்ல" என்று அமெரிக்க தளபதியின் முகத்திற்கு நேராகவே பேசி, இந்திய விமானப்படையின் தன்னாட்சியையும் சுயமரியாதையையும் நிலைநாட்டியுள்ளார் நமது ஏர் சீஃப் மார்ஷல்!

💬 உங்களுடைய கருத்து என்ன?
அமெரிக்க தளபதியிடம் நேரடியாக F-35 அணுகுமுறையைக் கிண்டலடித்து வெளுத்து வாங்கிய இந்திய விமானப்படைத் தளபதியின் இந்த அதிரடிப் பேச்சை நீங்கள் எப்படிப் பார்க்கிறீர்கள்? இந்தியா ரஷ்யாவின் Su-57-ஐ வாங்க வேண்டுமா அல்லது சொந்த தயாரிப்பான AMCA திட்டத்தில் மட்டுமே முழு கவனம் செலுத்த வேண்டுமா? கமெண்ட்டில் தட்டி விடுங்க! 👇

🚀 இந்தியப் பாதுகாப்புத் துறையின் இந்த கெத்தான மற்றும் துணிச்சலான போர்க்கள அப்டேட்டை உடனே உங்க நண்பர்களுக்கும் வாட்ஸ்அப் குரூப்களுக்கும் SHARE பண்ணுங்க! தொடர்ந்து உலக நடப்புகளையும் டிஃபென்ஸ் அரசியலையும் எந்த ஒளிவுமறைவும் இல்லாமல் தெரிந்துகொள்ள பக்கத்தை FOLLOW பண்ணுங்க! ❤️

text:
Chapter 4 (part 1) of Dark Cycle (My Malfoid fic)

"The Castle"

Bodies. All Draconia can see in front of her are bodies.

Students lying, back or front, down in the dirt. An empty void left in their gaze. Two more of her friends, about to die. She had already watched Goyle do the same. Death Eaters sending hexes, students firing return volleys. People running, some crying over fallen comrades and loved ones. A severed arm. A half missing its top. Slytherin robes. Flies have begun to swarm. Skirmishes, yelling, screaming, crying. Chaos. Pure, unbridled chaos has consumed the grounds of Hogwarts.

‘Is this real? Am I dreaming?’ She can hear her own voice, but her mouth isn’t moving.

She blinks, the world is slowed, time is near-frozen. Turning her head, she gazes upon the clambering silhouette of Neville Longbottom as he’s winding a swing.

‘Oh, right. We were going for a snake’s hea-‘

“DAMN IT, MOVE!” A yell rocks her out of her stupor.
Neville quickly pushes Draconia out of the way, Sword of Gryffindor elegantly swishing through air with practically zero resistance, the snake's neck doubly so. A loud hiss. The sound of whimpering. The sound of sizzling meat. Black mist fills the air as the body slowly begins to decompose rapidly into nothing. A triumphant yell sounds throughout the hall as Draconia frantically reaches forward to grab the shirt of one Hermione Granger.
“Come on, grab Weasley-“ They barely have time to react.

A voice penetrates deep into the recesses of her mind, inescapable, ethereal. Her grip loosens, sending Hermione back to the ground. It’s a whisper, serpent-like in cadence. Raspy, like a wire brush scraping against a screen mesh. Goosebumps raise across her body. She knows the voice well.

“You have fought well. You all have.” His voice reverberates off of the inside of her skull, bouncing around as a pinball would.

It’s him.

“I will recall my forces, and allow you to collect your dead. You have my word, you will not be harmed. Hold your loved ones close, you might find them gone soon.”

Harry. Where’s Harry?

“Harry Potter. I speak now, directly to you. You have allowed so many to fight and die for you. You have allowed so many to shield you from me.”

Her eyes dart around, Ron’s comforting a huddled Hermione, Neville looks like he’s about to cry. Several first years are comforting each other at the bottom of the staircase. No sight of him. No, no. He better not-

“I offer you this. No more magical blood needn’t be spilled. No more people have to die. Meet me in the Forbidden Forest and I will leave Hogwarts untouched. Come alone. You have one hour.”

Silence. Panicked footfalls. The chatter slowly returns to the building, more urgent and fleeting than before. A few hexes fire in the distance. She turns back towards Ron, her face full of concern. She’s seen better days, her outfit is ripped in various places, she’s covered in scrapes. Ron and Hermione aren’t doing much better having just survived the Chamber to destroy that damned chalice.

“Where is he?”

“I don’t bloody know, Malfoy, he was heading towards Ravenclaw tower last I saw him.” Ron sounds annoyed, as if answering her will somehow make Hermione’s condition worse.

“We need to find him Ron, knowing him, he’s going to actually fall for that. It’s obviously a trap of some kind-“

“He most likely knows that.” Neville speaks up.

“He’ll go anyway. You know just as well as we do, when it comes to us, he’s a reckless bastard. No matter what we tell him, he won’t listen. Voldemort’s scared. He knows we just need one more and he’s finished.”

Draconia clenches her jaw, her usual professionalism and class are completely absent. Her hair is a frizzled mess, every inch of visible skin caked in either blood or mud. She’s missing an earring.

“Damn him!” She slams her fist into the floor before collapsing beside Ron.

“What do we do, Weasley?”
“Why the hell are you asking me?”

“You’re Harry’s second in command or whatever. Surely he told you-“

“He hasn’t told me shit. He just said ‘the crown and the snake’, we have no Earthly idea what it could be.”

Her eyes lower to the floor below them, watching random students as they rush and leave the various parts of the hall. ‘Where could he be?’ is the only question on her mind as she stands up to help move the wounded.

“Let’s go, Neville.” she barks, Neville quickly reeling to follow as hastily as he could manage.

Harry Potter stands up, disorientated. His head is pounding, his scar is burning, vision blurry. He heard just like the rest. Students pay him no mind as they rush about the staircase, he begins to start down. Each step is a chore, each student bumping into him is a knife to the gut, another person he needs to save. Where is she right-

‘Don’t. Don’t do that to yourself.’ he thinks.

‘She’s fine. She has to be. She will be.’

Of course he’s going. He has to, what choice does he have? Is it a trap? Most likely. Will Voldemort keep his word? Certainly not. Time is what he’s after. More time for the school to rally, more time for them to live. If it means he has to die…

The bottom step is reached. His legs feel full of lead. Heavy. Too heavy. He soldiers on. He moves towards the corridor to the Grand Entrance. Another thought occurs. They have one last Horcrux to find and absolutely no idea what the Hell it could even be. Dumbledore left absolutely nothing in terms of information. He’s going in blind. He reaches and opens a heavy door, his footsteps echoing through the empty passage. Dying. Punching his ticket, kicking the bucket. At the hand of the one who took his parents that fateful night 17 years ago. He can feel himself trembling, his stomach acid rising in the back of his throat. Hands clammy, cold. Numb. He remembers the feeling of hers in his. How warm she is, how her touch feels like home. Why is this happening? Why is he doing this to himself? Why doesn’t he run and find her, run away from all of this? Years have been building to this, he knew that. He had always secretly hoped it would never come to pass.

Another door, closer now. He’ll have to take another exit, too many people might try to stop him. She might try to stop him. He wouldn’t have the heart to tell her no. He stops at a wall, a door slowly morphing from the stone, rippling like water, until it fully materializes in front of him. He grabs the knob and turns, pushing inward and entering the Room of Requirement. What’s left of it.

Burned and singed remains of books, desks, papers, and other miscellaneous school supplies are scattered around in a haphazard mess. The stench of burnt books, wood and flesh swirl into a putrid mixture that forces Harry to contain a gag. He pulls his shirt over his nose as he walks forward towards the back. Out of the corner of his right eye, he spots Goyle. What’s left of him.

He reaches a portrait, miraculously untouched by the flames and brilliant in color as if it were painted yesterday. A painting of Ariana Dumbledore. The passage they used to get here from Hogsmeade.

“Don’t tell Aberforth, please. I need to do this alone.”

He speaks to the woman, she studies him skeptically before giving a slight nod and swinging the portrait out, revealing the tunnel, stretching far along into darkness. He reaches up, hoists his weight and climbs in, making sure to crouch slightly before beginning the trek. The tunnel has been enchanted back when Dumbledore’s Army still operated in the school, making the distance much shorter than it is in reality. Regardless, it still feels endless to Harry. Step. Step. Step. No echo, it’s too cramped. A puddle soaks his shoe. He ignores it. A cobweb sticks to his face, he ignores it. One thing is on his mind and it’s not his impending demise.

After what feels like hours, he finally reaches the other portrait at the end of the tunnel, it swings open automatically and the familiar site of Hog’s Head Inn fills his field of view.

Voldemort is growing impatient. He knows Harry, he knows how stupid he can be when it comes to his friends. Around him, Lucius and Narcissa Malfoy, Wormtail, Yaxley, Macnair, and more. Hagrid stands away to their right, in chains, face low and bleak. He didn’t need them there, he could handle the child alone. He wanted them there so everyone could see him end Harry Potter permanently. No doubt, no room for tricks. Quick and clean, it will be done. As the minutes tick by and no sign of the boy has yet to materialize, the possibility begins to look dubious. He speaks, his voice commanding and steady.

“Wormtail, make preparations to resume the assault.”

“R-Right away, Master… Your will is my action…” Peter scurries towards Voldemort, eager to kiss or touch his hand. He takes hold, nearly slobbering in his fervor. Voldemort stares in disgust.

“Filthy abomination, begone with you.” His voice sibilant and annoyed, he snatches his hand back with an indignant flourish and watches as Wormtail fades into the mist of the Forbidden Forest. He’s a rat. A horrid wretch he wished he could be free of if he wasn’t so loyal.

Snap goes a twig. Leaves rustle and crunch under approaching footsteps.

Voldemort’s head swivels forward, the familiar sight of one Harry Potter gracing his view as he walks forward through the underbrush. His mouth curls into his signature merciless grin, cracked and yellow teeth glinting in the moonlight.

“Harry Potter.”

Harry doesn’t speak as he approaches, his face cut from granite and expressionless, finally picking a spot and standing opposite of Voldemort. His wand is already drawn, down by his side in his right hand. Hagrid immediately looks up, his face filling with sorrow and coiling into a face Harry hasn’t seen since Aragog’s funeral. He calls out.

“Harry- no! NO! What are you doing-“

“Silence, you impudent troll.” Voldemort hisses snidely, urging Yaxley to kick Hagrid hard in the side. He barely moves but obeys as large droplets begin to fall from his eyes. Voldemort swings his head back to Harry, his voice returning to its previous exuberance.

“The Boy Who Lived, has come to die.”

Harry again doesn’t speak, he just stares dead ahead directly into Voldemort’s eyes. He reminds him of his father, the spitting image of James. How he enjoyed watching life leave his eyes. Voldemort is nearly gleeful at the thought of reliving that night before he remembers what happened to him. He braces himself and raises his wand. Harry does the same. Moments pass, a twisted respect between the two shines through and they exchange a slight bow. Acknowledgment. They both speak at once.

“Expelliarmus!”

“Avada Kedavra!”

Red and green flash, clash then… white. Pure white.

Harry blinks. Nothing, then something. He’s confused. He’s standing in some kind of train station. He swiftly recognizes it. He was just in the forest, wasn’t he? Why’s he at King’s Cross? He takes a hesitant step, not even sure if he’s really here. Solid ground meets his foot. He takes another, then another. He’s walking now. A figure begins to take shape in front of him. Step. Step. Ever so closer until he can make out the form of-

“Professor Dumbledore?” Harry asks weakly, seeing none other than the departed headmaster sitting on a bench, waiting and staring ahead blankly. He seems to snap from some kind of trance, turning his head to beam up at Harry with a warm, familiar smile.

“Ah, Harry. So good to see you.” His eyes shine with his patented glimmer. His voice, chipper but restrained. Harry isn’t in such high spirits.

“What are you doing here? I-I saw you…” He trails off, unsure how to end that particular sentence.

“Where are we, Professor?”

Dumbledore looks around for a second, eyes tracing the girders and beams that line the ceiling.

“King’s Cross Station by the looks of it.”
“I can see that but… why?” Harry looks at him quizzingly.
“I would imagine to catch a train.”

Harry swallows a hard lump. Those words rattled him for some reason. They feel uncanny.

“Am I… dead?”

Dumbledore doesn’t take more than a few seconds to respond.

“It would appear that way, yes.”

Harry’s eyes drop slightly before sighing and finally taking a seat next to Dumbledore, leaning back into the bench to stare at the white ceiling above him. It appears almost transparent, nothing but a white void beyond the confines of the station. Dumbledore allows a moment to sit before he speaks again.

“I wonder to myself, what should we do with him?”

Harry’s brow furrows. He looks towards Dumbledore.

“Him, Professor?”

“Indeed, just look.”

Harry raises his head and looks toward Dumbledore. He’s pointing forward. Harry’s eyes follow his arm to its destination and nearly gasps in shock. Under the bench in front of them is a shriveled, bloody corpse. Corpse is a bit apt, it seems to be alive. Just so. It’s loud breathing ragged, skinny as a rail, its bones seem to struggle against his skin, begging to come loose. Harry didn’t even notice it breathing until he saw it.

“What the hell is that… creature, Professor?”

Dumbledore smiles again.

“You really don’t know?”

Harry gulps again. A knot forms in his stomach. He does, he’s always known. It’s the only possible explanation that makes any sense as to why he and Voldemort share such a… personal connection.

“It was me. I was the last Horcrux.”

“One I don’t think he intended to make, however.” Dumbledore pauses, turning his attention back towards Harry’s face. His warm smile returns.

“Funny thing, really. For one to tear his soul so many times that he didn’t notice when he created one in you. At least until it was too late. It’s a bit… silly. Even so, he just ensured that part of him will soon meet its demise.” Dumbledore motions to the body currently wheezing under the bench.

Harry looks back to Dumbledore.

“Professor?”

“Hm?” Dumbledore’s expression softens.

“What should I do?”

Dumbledore for the first time since they’ve begun talking drops his smile. He speaks with a serious tone, all feeling seeming to have drained from his inflection. The air seems to go still around him.

“There’s an old, black train coming, Harry. When it arrives, whatever your choice, do not get on it.”

Harry begins to speak but finds his voice muted. Lips move, no sound. Dumbledore watches, expressionless. He doesn’t speak, staring into Harry’s eyes with a haunting emptiness. Sounds in the distance arise, steadily increasing in volume. Scraping, a train approaches. Iron clanking, gears screeching, a loud and haunting whistle-

Draconia shakes her head in fear. Ron and Hermione flank her, Neville close by. Everyone’s gathered in the courtyard; the wounded have been moved to the Great Hall. On the road ahead, they see the group approach. Death Eaters. All of them. Their dark army follows in close proximity, full of every sentient magical creature they could persuade to their side. Voldemort is leading the march, nearly dancing his way across the stone. The fact they’re here can only mean one thing and there’s no way she could possibly prepare herself to see it. She spots Hagrid in his wake. He’s clutching something to his chest. She sees an arm loosely hanging from a gap in his own. A hole begins to form. Her chest crunches. It can’t be him. It has to be someone else.

“Neville… who’s that- who’s in Hagrid’s arms?” Her voice begins to waver, picking up in vibrato on the verge of tears.

Neville doesn’t answer, eyes glue ahead just like everyone else.

“N-Neville? Please don’t tell me it's-“ she cuts herself off. They’ve stopped walking.

The march concludes with the mass converging on the grounds, spreading out like fettered mud to block off any remaining exit. Voldemort steps forward, a sadistic smile painted to his grey, leathery face. He speaks in a delighted shout.

“Harry Potter… IS DEAD!”

Time stops. His words echo through her, tearing through her like a bullet, hitting every vital part of her being. Her throat dries, an irregular discomfort begins to flood into her. She can’t- is the world falling? Her feet- she can’t feel them. Spinning, everything’s confusing. Nonononono, this isn’t- She feels faint. Legs buckling. Collapse. Rubble crunches. Her hands clasp wildly at the ground, reaching, pleading for something to stabilize her; her nails scrape against the ground in vain as she finds nothing. A tenderness swells, an indescribable stabbing agony that rips her soul straight through her chest. She can’t hold it in anymore. She breaks. A sob, her knees are her only companion as she grips them tightly. She wants to bury her face in his chest, she wants to hold him, she wants to make everything as it was. She wants-

“Now then!” Voldemort claps his hands together. She doesn’t bother to pay attention.

“We are currently down in numbers, as you all well know. You gave us a Hell of a fight. Well done.” Voldemort begins to pace, using his wand to meagerly move a deceased student in his path.

“This is your opportunity to repent, and pledge your undying loyalty-“ he motions and points at his chest with his wand.

“To me.”

Silence, save for a small crash as another few bricks come toppling from Hogwarts’ foundation.

“Anyone? Any takers at all?”

Again, no response. Draconia’s still staring at the ground. Her father’s voice shakes her to awareness.

“Draconia.”

Sharp, desperate. She’s never heard his voice so… urgent. So despondent. Her head raises, her eyes tracking the ground until she spots him. He’s standing with her mother in his left arm, his right outstretched and waiting for her grasp. She doesn’t move to stand.

“Draconia, come. Please.” His eyes are to the ground as well.

She stands. She begins to walk. She doesn’t know how.

‘Why am I moving? Stay put, damn you.’ Her thoughts are loud in her head, practically screaming.

She’s numb, disoriented. Her steps lacked the usual refined demeanor she’s known for. She stumbles briefly before being welcomed by Voldemort himself. He smiles greedily, wrapping his arms around her. He’s stiff, inhuman, like he’s never hugged anyone in his life before this moment. She flinches, the man who ended her world is touching her. His skin feels like leather, his breathing is cold and shallow. He smells of death, like a rotting animal. Her face curdles at the sensation.

‘Disgusting. You’re disgusting.’ She wishes she could say it aloud.

“Well done, Draconia. Well done.” he looks past her to the crowd, threatening them as slyly as he could, his wand pointed menacingly. Everyone whose path it crosses cowers behind whatever they can find around them.

Release. He’s allowed her from his grasp. Tears well, she practically sprints to her parents. Lucius welcomes her first as she throws herself into him, stifling her cries into his chest. He cradles his only daughter, holding her tightly. A million differing apologies swim through his mind, none of them would ever be enough. Voldemort ignores them completely.

“Anyone else? We have plenty of-” Another steps forward. Neville this time. Nobody makes any attempt to stop him.

“I suppose I did say anyone, didn’t I? I can’t say I’ve had worse.” Voldemort sneers, the crowd behind him immediately swelling with mocking jeers and insults. He raises his hand to signal for quiet, they obey instantaneously.

“What might your name be, young man?” His voice has a cancerous sarcasm, one Neville can pick up on promptly.

“Neville. Neville Longbottom.” The Sword of Gryffindor hangs from his belt, shimmering in the afternoon glow. Another wave of laughing and mocking shouts flies his way before Voldemort raises his hand once more, silence falling quickly.

“Well, Neville, I’m certain we can find a place for-”

“I’d like to say something.” Neville stares dead into his eyes, not a flicker of fear on his face. Voldemort almost looks surprised he cut him off.

“I…” Voldemort goes to speak, thinks to himself for a moment, smiles and continues.

“I speak for all of us when I say we’d be delighted to hear what you have to say, dear boy.” Voldemort’s voice is clearly more amused than interested. He wants to see where this goes.

‘Arrogant bastard.’ Neville muses to himself in his head.

“It doesn’t matter Harry's gone.” he begins.

Draconia has to restrain herself from screaming, the reminder of his fate is too much for her to handle.

“Stand down, Neville.” Seamus Finnegan crudely whispers.

“People die everyday, Seamus. It’s no different from who we’ve lost already. Friends, relatives, lovers. We still get up, go about our days, life moves on…”

His head swivels towards the small crowd behind him.

“But we don’t. We remember. We’ll always remember who they were and what they gave for us.”

His gaze returns.

Voldemort raises a patch of skin where an eyebrow used to reside, this is tedious, sure but entertaining nonetheless. He’ll wait for him to finish before he slaughters everyone else in front of him. He’ll save him for last.

“They didn’t die in vain. Their sacrifice is the only reason we stand defiantly before you now.”
Neville’s face sours, twisting with anger; malice and loathing bleed from his stare. Voldemort’s almost impressed. He spits his words out with a vitriol none of them thought he was capable of producing.

“But you will. You’ll die screaming, begging for mercy, we will never stop-”

Voldemort begins to laugh, they can’t actually believe there’s still a chance in Hell they’re walking away from all this. This school will be their collective tomb by dusk.

“-we will never break! Harry’s heart beat and bled for us! We’re not LYING DOWN TO DIE!” He draws the Sword from his belt, holding it ready.

Voldemort raises his wand and prepares to fire the first volley when suddenly, sounds of struggle to his left. Sounds of cloth. Chains rattling. Hagrid gasps. The sounds of shoes hitting stone. It can’t be-

Harry’s awake and has begun running, his shoes heavily hitting the ground as he sprints off towards the destroyed bridge that once connected to the forest. Voldemort can hardly believe his eyes when another quick dash of white sprints past him. A flourish of hair, clicking boots hitting gravel. Draconia has also started running in his direction. The insolence. The nerve. The-

Crack. One of the Death Eaters surrounding him suddenly apparate. Crack. Another. Three more. Like the sound of popcorn, they rapidly begin to exit at the same time. Voldemort cannot contain his rage anymore, his wand readied on Draconia’s back.

“AVADA-”

“Flippendo!”

Thwack. A spell collides with his back, Voldemort flies face first into the rock below, his snakelike nose immediately leaking blood onto the rubble under him. Bright red paints the ground. The voice he heard cast the spell, it can’t be. He wouldn’t dare-

Lucius stands above him, wand drawn but shaking. He can’t believe he’s acting himself. He turns his head to Narcissa, his voice hurried and shaky.

“Narcissa, dearest, run and find-”

Green streaks across the courtyard, hitting Lucius square in the breast. A gasp. Light quickly fading from his stare briskly with a single tear passing down his cheek. He falls. First to his knees, then backward, face to the sky and body spread-eagle. Dead. Voldemort is on his back, wand pointed, wearing a satisfied expression. Narcissa shrieks, instantly apparating and fleeing like the rest. She appears to have splinched herself in her panic, small bits of flesh and hair remain where she once stood. Can’t focus on that now. Need to kill the boy.

Draconia’s panting, she can hardly keep up. They ran and ran, finally stopping near the clocktower. They take but a moment to catch their breaths before continuing on in a haste.

“Harry- where are we going-?”

“We need to lure him into the open. He’s alone, his forces broken. He’s going to be panicked and reckless, not willing to think things through. We need to bring him back to the courtyard after he catches up.”

“Then what? Everyone’s busy trying to get away from him, they’ll never help us-”

“I don’t know, damn it! This is the best I could come up with on such short notice- I should be dead right now, I haven’t had long to plan!”

He thinks a moment and calms himself.

“I’m sorry, I’m working with what we have-”

A loud crack. Out of time. In front of them, he appeared, absolutely furious, wrath oozing from every pore on his decrepit form. This is the second time Harry’s cheated death at his hand. Not again, he’ll kill them both. Slowly. Make them watch each other slip away. It’s only fair. She’s never truly been on his side. He knew it the whole time but to flagrantly rebel and raise her wand? Unforgivable.

“CRUCIO!” He roars, green lightning firing from his wand.

“Protego!” Harry raises a protective ward, allowing Draconia to return fire. He’s struggling, the Elder Wand is as formidable as they say but something’s off. Something feels unstable.

text:
Chapter 3 (part one) of Dark Cycle

"The Manor"
______________________________________

“Move your feet or you’ll lose them.”

A heavy hand smacks against the back of Harry’s head sending streaks of white though his already clouded vision. Woozy. Face hurts. He shakes his head. Not the biggest issue right now.

They’ve been captured by snatchers. By bloody snatchers. Muggle-hunting washups that look like charred shit and smell even worse. It’s a cruel joke. Out of everything that led to this, Harry Potter will die because of the scent of Hermione’s perfume. His hands are bound behind his back, Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger following closely behind in a similar state. Their faces are hollow, gaunt. It’s obvious to everyone they haven’t been living in the best conditions these last few months. His face suffers another pang of blinding pain. It’s swollen, tender, not quite right. Smack. Bars rattling. Fleeting stars shine through his darkened vision. Fenrir Greyback has shoved his head square into the barred gates of Malfoy Manor. The ghoulish appearance of Bellatrix Lestrange soon rushes over to greet him before she realizes who’s calling. Her expression sours. No smile, no theatrics, no semblance of care for his existence at all. Narcissa is behind her. Silent, watching.

“Piss off, Fenrir. We don’t want your lowborn filth at this proud estate. We sent you and your lot away for that very reason.” Her voice is lacking the usual sadistic flare she’s known for, she’s speaking purely business. As one would order a meal or schedule a dentist’s appointment.

“Ah, but Belly-Belly-Bella, don’t fret. We’d never bring you one if they weren’t special.”

Fenrir flashed his signature toothy grin, the hand he was using to hold Harry quickly makes its way down to his forehead.

“For starters…”

A calloused hand roughly slides across Harry’s forehead, scratching him slightly and forcing the tiniest drop of blood trailing down. Fenrir is quick to the cut, finger diving to scoop it from his skin and greedily wiping it across his top gum. A borderline orgasmic shudder runs through him. With his hair parted, the signature lightning bolt scar shines like a beacon. Bellatrix’s aura instantly shifts, her eyes growing wide with a mad delight and her twisted grin returning to its usual home. She almost can’t contain her glee but she calms slightly. Her voice is but a whisper.

“Get. Draconia.”

The gates slowly open, the towering and impressive architecture of the place would be seen as stunning if it weren’t for their current predicament. Bellatrix does an about face, skipping along ahead like some sort of demented schoolgirl, Narcissa following in tow with a muted grace. The path is impeccably paved, not a single leaf visible on the tiled concrete leading up the front stairs. ‘Typical Malfoy decadence.’ Harry thought as the snatchers led them along. Step. Step. Step. Step. They’ve stopped. Two large doors rest at the top of the stairs. Bellatrix doesn’t knock, they’ve already started opening for the group to funnel through.

The foyer is, in a single word, breathtaking. Unrepentantly lavish, indescribably fancy, so many family heirlooms and baubles adorn the walls and shelves lining the entryway. Too many to process, let alone count. Paintings of what can only be assumed to be past Malfoys and members of the House of Black hang all around them. Before anybody can take their first step, a discordant chorus of voices takes hold. True to their name, the paintings have all begun to hurl various obscenities and slurs towards the group. Mudblood, blood traitor, dung licker and worser unmentionables decorate the air as cleanly as the rest of the house.

“QUIET!” Bellatrix shrieks, her wand quickly removed from her pocket, a tiny flame appears from the tip of her wand like she flicked a lighter open. Nearly every painting soon goes quiet within seconds.

“Better!” She beams up at the paintings before turning about to face the group.

“Sissy! Come here, I need you to see this!” Bellatrix barks, her voice reverberating so loud it tickles Harry’s eardrums. He twitches his already swollen eye before slyly looking to his right to glance at Ron. He’s terrified. White as a ghost, which accentuates his already fiery red hair and freckles. His bottom lip is quivering. It was his fault they were here. He told them he had to do this alone. He warned them he had to do this alone. No dice. Through 7 long years, the three have been inseparable, through every danger, every test. They’ll make damn sure they’re inseparable in their deaths as well. Why does this always happen? His parents. Sirius. Mad Eye. Dumbledore. Death follows Harry Potter everywhere he goes, it’s his oldest friend since birth. It’s only natural to expect it.

The clack of heels against hardwood is heard as she moves closer. Clack. Clack. Clack. A frown begins to grow on her lips, she’s held her tongue since the gate. She meekly approaches Bellatrix, tentatively whispering in her ear.

“Bella, are you mad or simply daft?”

“I… what?” Bellatrix’s glee soon trickles into a confused amusement.

“You can’t bring these people here, look at them for God’s sake. This is our family’s ancestral home, you must be completely out of your goddamned-“

“It’s him.” Bellatrix grins.

Narcissa stops mid sentence. Her eyes widen just as Bellatrix’s did before but with a different emotion. She looked akin to a deer caught in headlights, her skin pale as fresh snow.

“Are you absolutely sure?”

“I can’t be. I’ve only seen him through pictures in the tabloids. Fenrir showed me the scar.”

“Well then why bring him here?” Narcissa darts her eyes to an entryway near the left side of the room.

“Take him somewhere for interrogation.”

“Draconia. Where is she?”

Harry’s heart plummets into Hell. He’s been catching glimpses, pieces of what they’re saying. Fenrir and Scabior have also gone quiet, eager to eavesdrop themselves in case they’re discussing their payment. Just quiet enough for him to hear her name spoken aloud. ‘She’s here, in the Manor.’ He thought. ‘If she still…’ he drifts. The last time they’ve spoken or even seen each other was in the clocktower where Dumbledore died. He’s been focused on the mission, focused on fulfilling his promise to Dumbledore. Goddamnit, how could he prepare himself for this?

“She’s in her chambers, shall I send for her?”

“YES!” Bellatrix hissed loudly, her temper growing with her impatience. “NOW!”

Narcissa flinches like an abused dog before meekly turning on her heel to start down the corridor, the now-familiar sound of her heels striding down the hallway with her. Bellatrix grins smugly before turning back to the other people she had been pretending weren’t there.
“Wonderful! Shall we retire to the den?”

Hard stone floor greets Harry and his friends as they’re thrown onto their stomachs, lined up like bucks on sale at a meat market. Harry’s lip slammed the hardest, a tooth directly embeds into his tender flesh. He was well acquainted with the taste of copper at this point, he paid it no mind. The best thing for Bellatrix would be confirmation. She gets the credit, she gets his praise, she gets to torture them. Only then will her prized pig be up for slaughter. Only with confirmation. This drives her crazy. Relatively. As crazy as one Bellatrix Lestrange could be if she were considered sane before. She grinds her teeth roughly, eardrums scanning carefully for any sign of-

Clack. Clack. Clack.

That wretched sound again. Every step fills Harry with more and more dread. It’s been almost a whole year. What if she’s turned completely? What if she’s different? What if she’s being coached, what if, what if. Her voice rings throughout his psyche. ‘Don’t die, Potter.’ What if she’s the one to do it?

Clack. Clack. Clack. The footsteps rise in rate, indicating multiple people on their way.

He turns slightly to shoot a glance at Hermione before a kick reaches the back of his head, sending him into the stone once more.

“No funny business, right? We can bloody see you a foot away.” Fenrir snarls, voice dripping with malice, looking for any reason to tear into the three of them.

Clack. Clack. Pause.

Harry can’t look, his attention glued to the grout lines of the floor.

“Grab him.” Bellatrix whispers, giddily bouncing over to the woman standing behind Narcissa. Lucius stands to her right, an authoritative aura exudes from his being, hand on his signature gold-tipped cane. Draconia slowly emerges, her steps light and graceful yet full of purpose. She’s draped in black, a fine and indulgent gown hugging her form perfectly. Pure giant spider silk, frilled pattern veils hang from her sleeves, while her shoulders are adorned in royal dark green patterns. Her makeup, immaculate as always. Her steps carry no hesitation as she walks over towards him, he still doesn’t budge. Her bright green heels arrive to fill his field of vision.

“Well? I’m not touching that creature.” Her voice is poised, filled with an annoyance rather than fear or venom.

Fenrir grabs the back of Harry’s jacket and shirt, savagely pulling him from his resting place and to his knees. Harry tries to look down, his head still glued to the floor before Fenrir grasps his hair and yanks. He can’t help but wince at the sight of her. She’s even more beautiful than he remembered. A shimmering oasis in the Hell they’re occupying. His broken nose and swollen eye do nothing to help his appearance, his breathing a heavy snort through blood and mucus. He coughs, sending a spittle of blood next to her shoe. She pulls it away in disgust.

“What am I looking at? You’ve brought me, what? Some kind of muggleborn servant?” She scoffs and rolls her eyes, looking back towards Bellatrix with an ardent intolerance. This is a waste of her time.

“Just who is this supposed to be?”

“Harry. Potter.”

She freezes in an instant. The refined and cold demeanor she had a moment ago appeared to crack briefly.

“P-Potter, you said? Harry Potter? ” She doesn’t turn to look back at him.

“We think. He has the scar. You went to school with him, you’d know him best.”

“W-Well those two there…” she motions to Ron and Hermione next to him, they don’t bother to look at her either.

“...are Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger. They’re his best friends… surely, he wouldn’t bring them with him to fight against The Dark Lord? They’re too precious to him-“

“I’m mad, not stupid, Draconia. Stop stalling.” Bellatrix grins widely. She’s not going to let her take a prize from her again. She won’t let her fail on purpose.
“Draconia. Think hard. Utilize tact. Do not make a mistake, this is more serious than you could possibly imagine.” The commanding voice of her father carries into her ears.

“I…” Draconia finally turns back to face Harry again. Eyes gliding across his face and body, studying every detail with a fevered precision. Her eyes finally meet his. Bright green mirrors itself upon their greeting. She goes pale, her skin growing cold immediately. She knows it’s him. Goddamnit, she asked him for one thing. One. Fucking. Thing. ‘You’re a complete and utter cretin, Harry Potter.’ She thinks to herself. ‘You’ve entered the House of Doom and decided to punish me doubly so by making me watch.’

She gingerly reaches out, brushing the hair from his forehead once more, a pointed finger trailing along that scar she’s seen hundreds of times before.

“Why’s his face… like that?” She gestures with her hands to circle his face.

Fenrir speaks up.

“Yeah, sorry ‘bout that. Must’ve hit him with a stinging jinx while we was trying to capture ‘em. Should be fine and pretty within an hour or so.”

Draconia’s eyes glimmer before she quietly tempers herself. She can’t get excited, show any relief. One bad reaction and she’s killed him.

“Put them in the dungeon then.” Hearing those words, Bellatrix lets out a rather unpleasant screech of defeat. Draconia angrily turns to her, growling in an unusually aggressive tone.

“Do you wish to explain why we’ve called The Dark Lord here if you don’t have what you promised?”

“Damn you, girl, you will NOT-“ Bellatrix takes a step forward.

“Do not speak to my daughter that way in this house unless you wish to lose your tongue, Bellatrix.” Lucius’s voice is steady and guided yet slightly flared.

“Do as she says.”

Bellatrix lets loose yet another guttural whine before looking at the three. As she steps towards them, something catches her eye. A glint of metal, hanging from Scabior’s belt.

“What is that?”

She points at the object with her wand. It’s a sword. A brilliantly ornate one. Rubies adorn the wrist guards, an even larger one in the base of the hilt. The unmistakable name of Goodrich Gryffindor is etched into the spotless metal.

“Oh this?” Scabior motions to his waist, lightly tapping the sword. His mouth grows a putrid smirk.

“The girl had it on her when we caught ‘em. I reckon we’ll take it as payme-“

“AVADA KEDAVRA!” The banshee shrieks.

A bright flash of green strikes Scabior square in the chest. His eyes shoot open before the air leaves his lungs and he falls back, eyeballs rolling up into his skull. Before Fenrir can even react, there’s a whip around his neck. Bellatrix lifts her wand, slowly raising Fenrir into the air as she does. He struggles, Harry can hear strained gurgles, gasps for breath. A sickening crunch. A loud thud.

“Bellatrix, ARE YOU MENTAL? ” Lucius roars. He storms over in a glide, lumbering over her by at least a foot. His voice drops to a deadly serious tone.

“Where do you get off murdering guests in my own home who may have helped us accomplish The Dark Lord’s will?” His face is a mix of angry, contorted and conflicted. Harry’s seen the same look on Draconia. Back in the lavatory.

“This little mudblood-“ she takes a few steps, stopping at Hermione’s side before she begins to prod her spine with the heel of her shoe. A small pop is heard. Hermione looks at Ron, eyes wide with horror. She doesn’t dare speak.

“Stole this from me. From my vault, Lucius.” She growls as she begins to apply pressure, Hermione quickly filling the room with panicked shrieks and beginning to thrash wildly. Ron fights hard against his restraints, screaming in a rage Harry’s only seen from that locket.

“I’LL KILL YOU, BITCH! DON’T TOUCH HER! FUCKIN- GET OFF HER! I’LL HAVE YOUR HEAD ON A PIKE BY DAY’S END, I SWEAR ON MY LIFE I’LL-”  His struggle covers him in abrasions, the enchanted rope around his wrist getting tighter with each failed escape.

Every word he bellows only makes her press in harder.
“Take these two below. I’d like to have a little chat with this one.” Her voice is disgusted, unimpressed. Almost bored. She finally withdraws her foot. Hermione pants and sighs in relief, not moving. Ron stops struggling but does not cease his glare. He doesn’t cease hurling obscenities. If looks could kill, she’d be atomized instantaneously.

“Girl to girl.”

Lucius looks over to the now lifeless corpses adorning the floor of his familial home. He looks at Ron flailing helplessly on his floor. He finally looks at Harry, curious as to why he’s just… laying there. It’s almost pathetic. This was Voldemort’s greatest threat? A  tired sigh escapes his lips as he wonders to himself. His eyes then drift back to Draconia. His eyes raise to Bellatrix.

“Fine. Make it quick.” Lucius moves towards Ron and Harry, stopping short of them. He draws his wand from the tip of his cane, lazily flicking his wrist and levitating the boys towards a gated doorway to their right. Another flick and it's open, the two writhing all the way down the stairs as they struggle in vain to break free from their restraints.

Chapter 2 of Dark Cycle (my Malfoid fic)
"The Clocktower" 
______________________________________

Dumbledore's voice is calm, tempered.

"Of course, I must ask. Why? You're not a killer, Draconia."

Draconia Malfoy is conflicted. Very much so. She's currently standing in the Clocktower of Hogwarts. Albus Dumbledore is staring back at her, her wand pointed directly as his chest. She's flanked on either side by Death Eaters. A voice hisses in her ear.

"Do it."

Everything's a blur. She feels faint. She's trembling. Is the room spinning? It's too fast, too soon. She wants to go back to the common room. To the Hall. To the last place where all that was swimming in her thoughts were test scores and him. Before her father forced this life on her, dropping it in her lap like a sack of bricks, forcing her to her metaphorical feet. Hogwarts was her home away from the manor. Yet here she is, betraying the only family that hasn't treated her like an accessory to their lineage. She feels scalded, her entire body scorching as beads of sweat begin to form. Burning, searing heat tears through her like her entire body is made of one muscle. Her left arm burns, her forearm throbbing in a searing heat. The familiar sting in the corners of her eyes forces her to focus.

"I have to... I was chosen... He chose me for this... I have to kill you..." Draconia's voice is hoarse and low, goosebumps prickling her skin as the words leave her mouth. She doesn't feel like the one speaking, she feels like a passenger in her own body. As if she's watching her actions being puppeteered by another. Eyes deadlocked onto him, she moves and grips the cloth on her opposite arm. She carefully rolls up her left sleeve, showing the unmistakable moving ink of The Dark Mark. A snake writhing inside a skull's mouth. Fitting for her situation.

"Come on, Draconia, do it!" Beatrix Lestrange barks her command with a demented elegance. Her voice quickly reigns itself, she's painfully aware not to scare Draconia anymore than she has to.

"Then we can call him... We can tell him everything... He'll be so proud of you..."

She's speaking softly now, it reminds Draconia of her mother. Her damned mother. Belatrix's frilly, black hair as well as her inflection bounce off the wind blowing gently through the open clocktower. Unpredictable as always. Various figures stand beside her, all apart of the dark army that invaded the school with Draconia's help. With her help. Albus is calm, restrained. A look, not quite readable, but without any hint of fear, is etched into his face.

"How did you come to invite your friends in such numbers? Surely, it couldn't have been easy. I haven't been able to quite work out how you've done it." he gestures with his blackened hand as he speaks. Just the reminder she needed.

Draconia puts on a feigned smirk, almost performative in its bravado. Her eyes betray her, she knows Dumbledore sees right through her act, clear as the crystal adorning his office. How many times has she stared him down in that wretched place? Always with the lectures, the talk of squandered opportunity. She's on the other side now, she's the one holding his fate in her hands. In her hands, she holds his life.

"Through the vanishing cabinet in the Room of Requirement." Her voice a rough snarl, empty bite. Her throat almost cracked near the end of her sentence. She knows he knows. Belatrix giggles quietly.

A glimmer shines through Dumbledore's eye that rocks her to her core. Is he... impressed with her? Did he want her to do this-?

"Ah yes. A silly oversight on my part. I could've never imagined you would actually assist these people, though. You had so much potential."

Anger. A seething anger bursts forth from inside of her, an involuntary roar like a cornered lion escaping her lips as she continues to tremble, her wand unable to stay still enough to find its target. A delighted jeer springs from Belatrix's black lips. Dumbledore's expression doesn't change.

"Do what you have to do, Draconia. Then The Dark Lord will reward you so handsomely..."

"I... I have to... do..."

Bad news. She's faltering. She's hesitating. This isn't going unnoticed by her compatriots and their patience is wearing thin. Fenrir especially, he grunts and begins to gnash his teeth. The Carrow Twins exchange a brief glance before straightening their gaze back towards her. Belatrix shoots him a deadly stare and he quickly backs down.

"It's okay, sweetie. It's okay, it's easy."

She muses, practically skipping her way to meet Draconia. She holds her close, her precious niece. Narcissa's spawn. Voldemort's chosen prodigy. Belatrix revels in her presence with a religious ecstasy, shaking wildly and voicing babble before a sinister seriousness appears within a blink of an eye. Her arm creeps up Draconia's, finding its resting place holding her hand, helping her to steady her wand.

"Just. Two. Words." A literal devil on Draconia's shoulder, hissing its wicked poison that her mind greedily injects. 'Yes.' she thought. 'It's just two words.'

Harry Potter can't process what he's seeing. Next to him, pointing his wand directly at his chest, stands the frame of Severus Snape. Harry struggles the understand the look on his face, he's gesturing to him to be quiet. A single finger placed to his lip, eyes braced with care yet full of worry. In all the time he's known the man, he has never seen a look remotely approaching the level of emotional vulnerability he's currently displaying. It's uncanny. Like a manakin was looking at him with longing. Above him, the woman he cares about more than all else about to kill the person he trusts the most. Harry's entire world has been inverted.

He can barely hear the conversation above, snippets from Dumbledore, Belatrix's unhinged tone. Nothing from her. He should stop her, every neuron in his brain is screaming at him to intervene and save both of them. He's the only one who can. Before he can even begin to move, Snape sharply pokes the wand deeper into his chest as if he could read his mind. He roughly shoves something into his arms. His invisibility cloak.

"DAMN IT, DRACONIA! DO IT! KILL HIM NOW!" Her voice is a sharp razor cutting into Draconia's psyche. Every sentence from her wretched mouth sickens her.

Belatrix's patience is wearing thin. Greyback's as well. Such a fine morsel sitting right in front of him and yet he cannot act. It's maddeningly delicious. Draconia's face contorts again, unable to utter the phrase to end this. To end him. Seconds go by painfully slow. Belatrix snarls, roughly letting her go with the same disgust you'd give a cockroach. Dumbledore watches in silence, his eyes tracking Belatrix as she moves throughout the room.

"Weak, weak, weak, weak, weak little snake."

Her voice is back to a chipper happiness completely alien to the moment before. She repeats her words enthusiastically like they're a ghoulish nursery rhyme she's just come up with as she skips around the room playfully.

Once more, Snape shoves his wand into Harry's chest before slowly beginning to turn. He doesn't dare move his wand nor his eyes before gesturing a second time to keep quiet. A footstep backwards, a turn, and he whisks himself up the stairs to join the rest. Harry clumsily throws the cloak over himself, watching the events unfolding above him in silence.

Snape emerges at the top step, pointedly looking to Belatrix with his usual abhorrence. He doesn't begin speaking until she stops skipping, finally looking towards him and tapping her feet impatiently.

"You dare question The Dark Lord's judgement, Belatrix?"

Snape's low, monotone voice cuts through the air. Almost immediately, every eye in the room turns its attention to him. Dumbledore's face, for the first time since this encounter began, flickers slightly. It's subtle, almost unnoticeable. Draconia notices. Harry notices. They've both spent years around this man, Harry has spent those years idolizing him as a surrogate father. He's scared, fear is in his visage clear as day to those with eyes to see. This rattles Draconia more than anything previous has. Why is he scared? Why is Snape here? Questions without answers abuzz in her mental space.

Belatrix hisses upon hearing Severus, her usual looney expression twisting into genuine anger at the implication her allegiances were anywhere else. She stomps her feet petulantly and puts on an almost comedically intense frown.

"Don't you ever question my loyalty, Severus. Some of us didn't go into hiding when The Dark Lord left us. Some of us didn't turn traitor."

"Then you'd do well to remember who his most trusted subject is, Belatrix. Especially when the information I provided him is the sole reason you're standing here right now." He doesn't blink, he doesn't take his eyes away from Dumbledore. He doesn't deign to look at Belatrix.

"Then do it. You took a vow." She hisses again before stomping her feet again, her frown turning to a twister sneer.

"Not... in front of the girl." His voice is careful, weighted. He's talking to one of the most unpredicatable people on the planet and he knows it. One wrong word and she'll go running to Voldemort, laughing all the while.

Belatrix looks confused, tilting her head in an exaggerated manner. Fenrir growls again, louder this time, causing Draconia to flinch. His eyes shoot to her and he flashes a sinister grin as if he's already sampling her flesh. His patience wears ever thinner. She doesn't dare to look in his direction. The Carrows both silently stare at her, not moving, not indicating any judgement, Death Eater masks glinting against the dim moonlight.

"What? Why not?" Belatrix huffs and crosses her arms across her chest like an overgrown toddler, face complete with a pout.

"For God's sake, Belatrix, look at her. She can barely hold her wand, much less do what needs to be done. She's not ready."

A demented laugh echoes throughout the wooden architecture, Harry grimaces. That same laugh echoed throughout the Department of Mysteries the night he lost Sirius. Throughout the field at the Weasley stack as he watched it burn. He'd hoped to never hear it again. He'd hoped to be the one to end it permanently.

"If she's not ready, she's not one of us."

"You question him again so brazenly. Surely, you'd wish to discuss this matter with The Dark Lord yourself, hm?"

Snape quickly rolls up his left sleeve, a daunting finger raised and held above his mark. Belatrix recoils like she's been hit with a hammer, her eyes drifting off to the side and crossing her arms in a childish pout.

"Draconia, wait below. I'll retrieve you myself, later."

Snape motions down with his wand, beckoning her downstairs. She doesn't move, her mind still spinning from everything happening. Snape once more motions, more urgent.

"Now."

This seems to bring her to a semblance of her senses. Her feet drag long and heavy across the wood, Harry watches her shadow grow larger with each step taken. Step. Step. She's on the stairs now. Step. Step. At the bottom, she finds herself alone. The empty room of the lower level stares back at her hauntingly. Her face grimaces and she finds herself holding back tears. A rustle. Her nerves steel themselves as she points her wand to the darkness. Not a word spoken. The sound of cloth moving. Her eyes dart around wildly before, finally, he appears. First his head, then the rest as the cloak falls to the ground. Their eyes meet, she has to stop herself from yelling in shock. Face to face, feet away, deadlocked on each other like predators about to fight. Something inside gives; she bolts forward as quickly as she can without making noise and throws herself into his arms. She grasps him tightly, fingers streaming through the hair on the back of his head as she desperately tries to remember his touch. She doesn't speak, she doesn't need to. He already knows. He holds her close, gently stroking her hair as he lays his cheek against the top of her head. Warm, he thought. She's so warm.

"Severus. Severus, please."

Three words shake them from their embrace. Three words spoken with fear. Neither of them have ever heard Dumbledore so vulnerable, so... mortal. It's terrifying. The two tear their focus from each other, as painful as it is to do so. Harry reaches down, slowly taking the cloak into his hand and throwing it over the both of them. He locks his eyes onto Snape through the thin veil. Draconia watches Dumbledore. Time seems to stand still around them before Snape raises his wand, leveling it as casually as if he were shooting a tin can. He speaks with a restrained emotion Harry can't quite place.

"Avada kedavra."

A loud bang followed by a fizzle, a flash of bright green light floods through the cracks in the wood above them. A gasp. Silence. All of the air disappears around them. Two sets of green eyes watch as the body of Albus Dumbledore topples from the window of the clocktower. Two sets of mouths are agape in pure hysteria. Two sets of arms hastily find their way back to each other. Two sets of green eyes, begin to weep. A silence sets in beside the sounds of their tears.

"No... I didn't... I had to..." one of them speaks, frantic and panicked. Frightened. Unsure. Harry can feel her fingers harden against the cloth of his robes, her grip like a vice. She can feel the guilt begin to compound unto her conscience. This was her fault. She approached him. She let the Death Eaters in. She helped them take the castle. She killed-

"It's okay, Draconia, it's okay... You didn't." Harry replies tenderly in sharp contrast to what his mind is screaming at him. He's angry. So angry he wants to charge up and kill Snape himself. He wants to torture him. Curse him, burn him, stab him, damn it, massacre him. He wants to make him suffer so much he'll beg him for death. A death he wouldn't grant for a long time. A soft whimper brings him down. He knows no matter how angry he is, it doesn't change that she's more hurt than he is. He knows how difficult this spiral has been for her, he's wanted to apologize since the bathroom. Since he hurt her himself. He wants to help, he wants to try. Giving up would be too easy but he knows she won't let him. Even if he wanted to.

'She's so warm.' He thought as she buries her face into his chest and lets out a quiet sob. That sinking feeling starts to creep into him with each passing second. He has to leave her soon, he knows that. Every muscle and sinew in his frame is fighting that fact, almost as if he's in a literal tug of war with his own body.

"I knew you weren't like them..." he whispers, his voice clearly strained from crying. He's back to lightly stroking her hair. She smells of lilac and misery, it's intoxicating.

"You don't know anything, Potter..." she whispers back, her reply equally as tense. She knows he has to go, she has to force him to. They'll kill him if they saw him. Or worse. The torture that awaits him at Voldemort's hand would be indescribable. She hurriedly buries the thought, she can't stomach it. The blood of a mentor is one thing. The blood of the man she loves is a completely different animal she can't possibly hope to deal with.

"You..." her voice cracks, as if she's forcing herself to speak. Her head doesn't move, her hands fiddle idly with his robe sleeve.

"You have to go..." Draconia doesn't raise her voice in the slightest. Her eyes drop, suddenly becoming very interested in the lines on the hardwood. One indication she's not alone and Fenrir will descend on them, feasting on their bones for dessert after thoroughly gorging himself of their entrails.

When her words reach his ears, Harry shakes his head defiantly and his form goes rigid.

"No- I won't. I'm not. I can't lose you too, please Draconia, come with me..."

His grip grows ever tighter on her robes, his arms locking like iron, he'd rather die than leave her now. Everything is about to get worse than either of them can imagine, he won't do it without her.

"Don't make me... please..."

His words are a toxin. Without malice yet full of venom. An addictive drug she urgently needs to quit. Her arms start to push, gently at first before quickly rising in strength.

"They'll kill you... do you want me to see that? Do you really hate me that much? You want to throw your life away and make sure I can't ever hold you in my arms again?" her voice is smooth, more composed. Still a whisper in his ear. Harpy. Speak your vile words elsewhere. He won't. He can't.

"I..."

He begins to speak but doesn't have a response. She pushes once more, successfully this time, forcing herself from his embrace. She doesn't step back, clumsily holding the cloak to ensure they're still hidden.

"Please, Harry... Go..." she finally looks up to stare at him, her green eyes dark with concern and regret. He's never noticed how much her eyes look like his. Before he can stop himself, before he recognizes his actions, he leans towards her. He clambers at her presence, trying to calm her briefly before planting a long kiss upon her lips. She freezes. Her shoulders raise for a time then lower. She melts. Her arms snake their way up his shoulders before stopping at his neck, holding him delicately. Another moment passes. They separate.

Harry somehow musters a tiny, weak smile before taking a step back. She instinctively moves her arms to reach for him but stops herself. Her face is burning red, ears tinged a soft pink. So many emotions, so little time to process. She hopes he can't see her in the low light.

"I'll- I'll come back for you... I promise."

Harry's words swim laps in her mind. The only way he'd be able to do that is if he... She doesn't finish the thought.

"Don't die, Potter... don't leave me on my own again... like before.."

Her voice is quiet as a mouse, even quieter than before. Her breathing is ragged, her head swimming with things she wished she could say to him, things she's been grappling with for years. An ironic catharsis floods her, she knows he feels the same. Step. Step. Step. Hurried falls of Death Eater feet begin to move towards the staircase. Harry's eyes widen before sprinting down the rest of the bannister, rushing haphazardly out to Dumbledore. A crowd has already gathered that he fights his way through before collapsing at his slain mentor's breast. His wails begin to fill the space outside.

Gone. Safe. For now. Her heart aches. She knows what awaits him. She'd wished she never come this year. Why did he come this year? She sabotaged him, she assaulted him, she broke his nose and yet he still pushed through.

The ghastly group quickly appears on the stairs behind her, filling the void Harry left.

"Come, Draconia, we must call him. Call The Dark Lord."

The voice is Snape's. He's outstretched his hand, urging her to take it. She looks at him with the same look one would give a dangerous, violent animal before calming herself and taking his hand into hers.

"Right..." she whispers, the howling laugh of Belatrix Lestrange harshly attacking her eardrums as they start down the bannister.
